Kim, Ben — I pulled the infra traces and here's what we see (summary):

1) Root cause signal: an autoscaler-driven binpack event in us-west-2 triggered a set of preemptible host evictions on the serving fleet. Multiple worker processes were rebalanced; during the reattach of KV-cache and warm-up the fronting process returned 503 for in-flight requests.

2) Impacted window: we observe intermittent 503s starting 2027-05-16T01:38:12Z with spikes until 2027-05-16T02:21:45Z. There is a continuous high-error segment from 2027-05-16T01:58:03Z to 2027-05-16T02:29:16Z where error rate exceeded our 99.9% availabilitySLO indicator for that customer's route. The longest contiguous unavailability segment by our definition is 1913 seconds.

3) Evidence: attached trace bundle (trace_bundle_20270516.tar.gz) and extracted server logs evanpay-service-logs-20270516.csv. I've marked node IDs and sample request IDs that correlate with the client's CSV.

4) Remedy eligibility: per the contract (Section 4.2 Availability) a continuous unavailability window > 15 minutes qualifies for a pro-rata availability remedy. For this customer and month, a pro-rata credit of 7.5% of monthly invoice is our suggested initial estimate. Finance/escalation can adjust for lost revenue figures, but this is consistent with previous similar events.

Action items:
- Marissa: can you prepare the credit calculation and client-facing wording (legal-approved) for the remedy?
- Ben: please validate the SLO timeline and produce the annotated SLO chart (slo-window-annotated.png) for the postmortem packet.

Attachments: trace_bundle_20270516.tar.gz (3.2MB), evanpay-service-logs-20270516.csv (1.1MB)

—Aditya

Alexa — thank you for your patience. Quick summary and next steps: 

Summary of findings (internal):
- Confirmed impacted window: 2027-05-16T01:38:12Z to 2027-05-16T02:29:16Z (contiguous high-error segment ~1913s).
- Cause: autoscaler binpack + preemptible host evictions in us-west-2 leading to worker warm-up delays and 503s.
- Evidence: we've attached server-side traces and annotated SLO chart.

Proposed remedy and timeline:
- Eligibility: based on Section 4.2 of our agreement, this event meets the availability remedy criteria (continuous unavailability > 15 minutes).
- Proposed credit: initial estimate 7.5% credit against EvanPay's May 2027 Redwood invoice. Marissa will follow up with the precise dollar amount and a formal credit note by EOD Wednesday.
- Postmortem: SRE will produce a public postmortem (redacted for customer PII) within 10 business days. We'll include mitigation steps and any changes to autoscaler thresholds to prevent recurrence.

Action items for EvanPay: please confirm you accept the proposed credit path and whether you'd like us to route the credit as a one-time invoice adjustment or as a billing credit for June. Once you confirm, Marissa will prepare the formal credit note and procurement@evanpay.com can sign off.

We're sorry for the impact here — we'll prioritize the postmortem and the credit flow.

Best,
